newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rise after economic data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rise after economic data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rose, with T-bonds breaking above the top of the range of the past two sessions, after U.S. economic data came in weaker than anticipated.
U.S. durable goods order fell 1.6 percent in November compared to expectations for a 0.1 percent rise. October orders were revised upward to up 0.5 percent from up 0.3 percent.
Jobless claims in the latest week, however, partially offset the positive durable goods orders figures, falling to 335,000 compared to expectations for a decline to 346,000 from a revised 350,000.
The March T-bond broke above the top of the week's range near 113-21/32 on the advance, sparking a bit of followthrough buying that pushed the contract to its daily high.
"There was a good seller in here, but it kept a good bid," said one T-bond futures trader on the floor of the Chicago Board of Trade.
Activity had been extremely quiet all week, both before the Christmas holiday and between the Christmas and New Year's holidays, but picked up after the release of the economic figures.
Resistance in the nearby T-bond contract is now evident near 113-28/32 to 114-00 and again near 114-06/32, floor traders said.

At 0749 CST, March T-bond futures were up 14/32 point at 113-25/32, 10-year T-notes were 7/32 higher at 109-28/32 and muni-bonds were 17/32 higher at 116-23/32. March IMM T-bills were two basis points higher at 94.98 and Eurodollars were two point higher at 94.47. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
